instrument: Siglent oscilloscope (SDS1000X-E / SDS2000X Plus / SDS800X HD / SDS3000X HD)
source: Transcribed from the Siglent SDS Series Digital Oscilloscope Programming Guide (EN11D, Feb 2023), with the SDS3000X HD guide (EN11F) adding the newer models. This is Siglent's modern standard-SCPI set; the first-generation SDS1000CML/DL and early SDS2000X take a different LeCroy-derived dialect (C1:VDIV, TDIV, TRMD) that is not covered here. Cross-checked against pymeasure siglent_sds1000xhd and teledyne_oscilloscope. Read back against the EN11D guide in August 2026, then against the EN11F guide for the SDS3000X HD models this catalog also covers. 25 of the 36 entries EN11D does not print are in EN11F, including :DVM, :COUNter, :MEASure:ASTRategy and :DISPlay:MENU:HIDE. :TRIGger:SENT:Source and :TRIGger:SENT:THReshold are in EN11F too — the :DECode:BUS<n>:SENT: commands in EN11D are a different subsystem, not the same command misfiled — The Source entries are written SOURce: that guide prints the node both ways, and its heading and its worked example both use SOURce while only the syntax lines use Source. Nine IEEE 488.2 common commands remain in neither guide: *CLS, *ESE, *ESE?, *ESR?, *SRE, *SRE?, *STB?, *TST? and *WAI. They are kept. Unlike the R&S manuals, which print an explicit list of the common commands they support and so make an omission meaningful, neither Siglent guide prints such a list — it documents *IDN?, *OPC, *OPC? and *RST where they happen to be relevant and says nothing either way about the rest. These nine are mandatory in IEEE 488.2, and removing mandatory commands because a vendor guide is thin would take away things that work.
